title: Build a Mac app that stays awake with the lid shut
summary: A non-developer had Factory's Droid build LidAwake, a free app keeping his Mac awake with the lid shut; he says it took about three hours, including a launch video.
agent_role: Droid did the research, build, tests and bug fixes, and produced the launch video (three.js MacBook, Python-generated music) and thumbnails. The human described the problem, switched the app on to test it and asked for fixes and the video.
outcome: Author reports a first version in 15 minutes and the finished app, video and thumbnails in about 3 hours of Droid time.
what_they_did: The poster, who says he is not a developer, wanted his coding agents to keep working with his MacBook lid closed. Apple's built-in keep-awake command does not cover that. He asked Factory's Droid to build a fix and got a first version in 15 minutes. He then had Droid find and fix bugs and make a launch video. The result, LidAwake, sits in the menu bar and shuts off if the battery runs low or the Mac gets too hot.
how_it_went: He says Droid did the research, building, testing, every fix, the launch video and three thumbnails in about three hours. The app is free on GitHub with a 12-step manual test plan.
worth_knowing: The app gives itself permission to change sleep settings and runs a background watchdog. An awake Mac is not necessarily online, and an agent stuck on a permission prompt or usage limit still stops. Don't run it in a bag.
prompt: I'm not a developer. Help me build a small [macOS menu-bar / desktop] app that solves this problem: [describe the problem]. First research why existing options like [existing tool] fall short, and propose a plan. Wait for my approval before changing any system settings or permissions. Build a first version, then write and run tests and fix any bugs you find. Document exactly what the app changes on my machine and how to uninstall it. Finally, draft a short launch video and [number] thumbnails. Show me everything before publishing anything.

curation.rationale: A self-described non-developer had an agent research, build, test and fix a working macOS utility, plus make a launch video and thumbnails. The open-source repo includes a detailed README and test plan.
